entries.title: Lamentations 2:1
segments:
vv 1-10. 
 
None can know the power of God's anger.  The nation that presumes to provoke him by persisting in transgression will find that he is able to visit it with calamity upon calamity, till its resources ae utterly exhausted, and it sinks in hopeless misery and ruin.

entries.title: Lamentations 2:3
segments: Hath drawn back his right hand from before the enemy; refused to use it against them, and thus allowed them to prevail.

entries.title: Lamentations 2:6
segments: Of a garden; which is only temporary, and is taken away when the fruit is gathered.

entries.title: Lamentations 2:7
segments: As in the day of a solemn feast; the number and tumultuous shouting of the enemy is compared to that of the Israelites assembled at Jerusalem to celebrate their solemn feasts.

entries.title: Lamentations 2:8
segments: Stretched out a line; measured out Jerusalem for destruction.

entries.title: Lamentations 2:11
segments:
My liver is poured; that is, my gall; the effect of excessive grief. 
 
As good men are the first to lift up their warning voice against the sins which destroy men's bodies and souls, so are they the first to mourn over the misery which men bring upon themselves by refusing to listen to reproof; they who have been most hated and persecuted for their faithful reproofs, often shed most tears over the calamities which these reproofs were intended to avert.

entries.title: Lamentations 2:12
segments: It is a universal law of God's providential government that none sin for themselves alone; they involve those who are connected with them in the consequences of their transgressions.  Especially does this law hold good in the relation of parents to children.

entries.title: Lamentations 2:13
segments: What thing--witness for thee; what example can I bring that shall meet thy case, and thus be a source of consolation to thee?

entries.title: Lamentations 2:14
segments:
Not discovered thine iniquity, to turn away thy captivity; not declared to thee faithfully thine iniquity, that so, by bringing thee to repentance, they might prevent thy captivity. 
 
  False burdens and causes of banishment; pretended communications from God, that flattered men in sin by lying words, and so became causes of banishment.  But others render, "false burdens and seductions," that is, seducing prophecies. 
 
The worst enemies of both nations and individuals are "false prophets," who flatter sinners with the hope of impunity in sin, instead of faithfully warning them of its guilt and ruin.

entries.title: Lamentations 2:15
segments:
vv 15-19. 
 
Good men mourn over the calamities which befall God's people, and pour out their hearts in prayer for their removal; but wicked men exult over them, and make them the occasion of blaspheming God's name.  By this test the friends and the enemies of God may be known.

entries.title: Lamentations 2:22
segments: Hast called--my terors round about; hast called together terrors against me on every side, as men are called together in a solemn feast.
